text:
sam: Pushed profiler traces from the MoE rollout on dedicated pool 3. Seeing 25-40% tail P99 increase for long-context chat workloads. Suspect all-to-all hotspots during token routing. attaching quick snippets and notes.

sam: pprof flame: top stacks are ncclAllToAll -> route_tokens -> compute_expert_forward -> cudaMemcpyAsync (lots of waits). GPU compute <=> comm overlap looks poor.

sam: snippet: `P99 latency: baseline 210ms -> rollout 290ms (+38%)`; `GPU util: avg 68% but stalls during routing windows`

anya: ugh. Is the regression isolated to MoE config only? or also seen on dense variants?

sam: only on MoE config (8 experts, expert_capacity=2x). Dense models unchanged. We rolled kernel selection changes last week that change kernel tiling for ffwds, but timeline aligns with MoE config and routing change to topk=2.

jyoti: can you paste NCCL timeline? curious about allreduce vs alltoall overlap.

sam: here's a condensed NCCL trace (not full):
```
[0.00s] compute batch A forward (0-120ms)
[0.12s] ncclAlltoAll start (120-180ms) -> stalls
[0.18s] compute resumes 180-240ms (partial)
[0.24s] ncclAlltoAll start (240-320ms)
```
Looks like repeated back-to-back all-to-all windows with little overlap.

mike: are we pinning routing buffers to CUDA pinned memory? dma stalls can show up like that.

sam: routing buffers are GPU resident but we memcpy to host for some metrics. There are extra host->device memcpy calls in the flame for routing bookkeeping. Might be our token routing debug path.

evan: kernel selection changes could've changed kernel launch concurrency (stream priorities). If kernels got serialized on the default stream, NCCL might not interleave. Did the rolling patch change stream usage?

sam: patch adjusted fused FFN kernel to use stream0 to avoid races. That likely serialized with NCCL which uses stream0 by default.

anya: that explains it. Quick mitigation: move NCCL ops to a dedicated comm stream or lower the FFN kernel to a non-default stream and use cudaEvent to sync only where necessary.

jyoti: also consider hierarchical all-to-all (group experts per socket) to reduce cross-switch traffic. For 8 experts across 4 GPUs, do local shuffles first then inter-node. Cuts latency if we can restructure expert assignment.

mike: batching heuristics could help too. If we micro-batch tokens by destination expert before routing, you reduce number of small all-to-alls. Think: do a lightweight bucketing pass to group token destinations for 16-32ms windows.

sam: idea: run token destination histogram per micro-batch and if skew detected, postpone some tokens or route to fallback dense path. We already have fallback variant for overload but not automated on per-batch basis.

evan: for long-term, change token routing to sticky routing (prefer same expert if token history indicates) to amplify locality. But that risks quality regression. Need evals.

jyoti: also check NCCL params: NCCL_ALGO=Ring vs Tree, NCCL_TOPO_FILE, NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS. For NVLink-heavy boxes, P2P=VIRTUAL or SYS matters. We should run microbenchmarks to measure alltoall bandwidth under current topology.

sam: i ran a small bench: alltoall bandwidth dropped ~30% vs baseline under synthesized traffic with current kernel patch. attaching raw numbers in a follow-up Gist.

infra-bot: perf-test/bench-alltoall job #472 failed threshold: bandwidth 14.2GB/s < expected 20GB/s (see CI link: https://ci/internal/472) :warning:

mike: for quick rollback, revert stream change in kernel patch and gate by a flag so MoE rollout can opt-out. We'll measure impact.

anya: agreed. Also try increasing overlap by launching NCCL ops earlier (issue async queues) and use cudaStreamWaitEvent to sync compute segments that truly need results.

jyoti: KV cache behavior: routing currently reorders KV cache writes across GPUs which forces an allgather-like sync for position ids. Could we shard KV by expert and keep writes local, applying remote patches asynchronously? That reduces sync windows. Needs careful correctness checks.

sam: good call. Currently we do flush+merge semantics on every step which is heavy. If we switch to eventual-consistent KV patches we might shave those stalls.

evan: small experiments to run: 1) revert stream->stream0 change (fast), 2) run NCCL_ALLTOALL microbench per box, 3) enable hierarchical alltoall in routing, 4) try topk=1 sticky routing on a canary traffic slice and run quality evals.

mike: i'll open a short-lived feature flag for kernel stream selection and roll it to 10% of traffic for the MoE pool.

sam: thanks. i'll push profiler traces and the pprof tarball to the thread Gist and link in 10m. also adding timeline screenshots.

anya: one more: check for small-message inefficiencies. Many all-to-alls with tiny messages are worse than fewer bigger ones. If batching heuristics can aggregate token payloads by destination, it's a big win.

jyoti: can we add a lightweight router that predicts destination distribution for the next token window and pre-allocates comm buffers sized accordingly? Might reduce realloc cost.

sam: noted. ok next steps documented: revert stream change -> smoke test; run nccl microbench; prototype micro-batching by destination; experiment sticky topk=1 on canary.

evan: thanks. please tag me when you flip the flag so i can watch traces. :eyes:
